title: IAS Couple Finds Insect in Salad at Upscale Gurugram Restaurant, Sparks Food Safety Probe
excerpt: Food safety officials inspected The House of Celeste and collected samples for laboratory testing after diners discovered a caterpillar in their vegetable salad.
body:
• An IAS couple found a live caterpillar in their vegetable salad at The House of Celeste, an upscale restaurant in Gurugram's Sector 15
  • Food safety officials inspected the restaurant and collected samples of paneer, cashew nuts, peanuts, and green chutney for laboratory testing in Karnal
  • The inspection revealed multiple hygiene lapses and no recent signs of pest control at the establishment
  • The restaurant, reportedly associated with Michelin-starred chef Suvir Saran, has been issued a formal notice demanding documentation within 10 days

Fine-Dining Meal Takes an Unsettling Turn

A luxury dining experience at one of Gurugram's high-end restaurants turned into a food safety nightmare when an IAS couple discovered a caterpillar crawling in their vegetable salad. The incident at The House of Celeste, located in Sector 15 Phase 2, has prompted a government investigation and renewed questions about hygiene standards at premium dining establishments across India's National Capital Region.

The couple, who chose to remain anonymous, recorded the insect moving through their peas and broccoli salad and immediately reported the matter to the restaurant management. According to Crosstown News, the initial response from the establishment was unsatisfactory, prompting the diners to escalate their complaint directly to the food and supply department.

"What we found was alarming."

— Ramesh Chauhan, Senior Food Safety Officer, Gurugram

Authorities Move Swiftly

Food safety officials acted within days of the complaint. Senior food safety officer Ramesh Chauhan led an inspection team to the restaurant, where they collected samples of paneer, cashew nuts, peanuts, and green chutney. The samples were dispatched to a government-approved laboratory in Karnal for comprehensive testing.

The inspection uncovered more than just the reported insect. According to OBNews, officials found multiple hygiene lapses at the restaurant and noted the absence of recent pest control measures — a significant shortcoming for any food establishment, let alone one positioning itself as a premium dining destination.

A formal notice has been issued to The House of Celeste, demanding pertinent documentation and a response within 10 days. The restaurant has denied the presence of any insect in its food, according to DevDiscourse.

A Pattern of Incidents

The episode at The House of Celeste is not an isolated case. India has seen a string of food contamination incidents at restaurants in recent months. In Punjab's Ludhiana, a boy was hospitalized after a lizard was found in a kulfi purchased from a street vendor. Bengaluru's Rameshwaram Cafe faced allegations of worms in food, though the restaurant claimed the incident was staged as part of an extortion attempt.

These incidents highlight a persistent gap between the premium pricing of upscale establishments and their actual adherence to food safety standards. India's Food Safety and Standards Authority (FSSAI) has ramped up inspections across metropolitan areas, but enforcement remains inconsistent.

What Diners Should Know

The House of Celeste, reportedly opened by Michelin-starred chef Suvir Saran in 2020, had positioned itself as a destination dining experience in the Gurugram market. Saran's continued association with the restaurant at the time of the incident remains unclear, and the chef has not made any public comment.

The complainants have opted not to pursue further legal measures at this stage, preferring to await the laboratory results before deciding on next steps. Final regulatory action will depend on the test outcomes from the Karnal laboratory.

For diners in Gurugram's competitive restaurant scene — where a meal at such establishments can easily run into thousands of rupees — the incident serves as a reminder that price alone is no guarantee of quality or hygiene.
nri_angle: NRIs visiting India frequently dine at upscale establishments in Gurugram and Delhi NCR, making food safety standards at premium restaurants directly relevant to diaspora travelers.
author: Diaspora Desk
